title: Active to Passive Voice: Rules and Verb Forms — Quiz 102A
content:
## Active to Passive Voice: Rules and Verb Forms

Review subject-object changes and passive verb forms across tenses.

### Lesson focus

1. Change the subject into the object and the object into the subject.
2. Use the third form of the main verb with the appropriate form of be.
3. Place by before the agent when it is needed.

### Understand the pattern

The new subject is the receiver of the action; the old subject, if needed, becomes the agent after by. Keep the active tense. Present simple uses am/is/are plus a past participle; past simple uses was/were; present perfect uses has/have been.

### Worked answers and explanation

Compare 'Mina writes the notice' with 'The notice is written by Mina'. For an action in progress, 'Mina is writing the notice' becomes 'The notice is being written by Mina'. Do not omit being, because it carries the continuous meaning.

### Try another

Change: They will announce the result tomorrow.

### Suggested answer

The result will be announced tomorrow. After will, use the base form be and then the past participle announced. The unspecified agent they can be omitted.
